::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**This is individual work.** Every student submits their own. The final project is where you work
in a team; the studio is where the mechanics get into your own hands.
:::

The session runs to a fixed clock: **Build** 25 minutes, **Use** 20, **Reconcile** 15, **peer check** 5.
The move from Build to Use is called at minute 30 whether or not Build finished — an unfinished
Build is a legitimate finding, reported as one.

::: {.part}
### Part 1 · Before you arrive

Accounts and data only. Nothing here needs software installed at home.

1. Download this week's dataset from the course Drive folder into your `IMSE456` cloud folder.
2. Open the week's Colab notebook and run the first cell to confirm it loads. Ten minutes, from any machine.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 2 · What you will have at the end

SA14 — the close-out package and the evidenced-lessons list, each lesson with its data citation
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 3 · Build it yourself — 25 minutes

1. Export your full Taiga history — stories, comments, issue transitions, timestamps.
2. In Colab, extract the timeline: where did items sit longest, which stories were reopened, when did scope enter?
3. Feed the <em>extract</em>, not your memory, to Gemini and ask for candidate lessons. Reject every one you cannot evidence from the data.
4. Assemble the close-out package: final schedule versus baseline, final EVM position, register with outcomes, evidenced lessons.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 4 · Now the professional tool — 20 minutes

1. In ProjectLibre, produce the final baseline-versus-actual comparison.
2. In Power BI, build the close-out dashboard: planned versus actual duration and cost, the register with outcomes, and the cycle-time trend across all sprints. One page, readable by someone who was not on the project.
3. Archive per the naming convention: <code>FINAL.pod</code>, the Taiga export, the Smartsheet export, the <code>.pbix</code>, and the report.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 5 · Where do they disagree? — 15 minutes

The lessons you remember versus the lessons the record supports. Which of your remembered lessons does the data contradict?

Write one paragraph. **This is the graded part** — it is the only thing here a machine cannot check.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 6 · Run the check

Run the `verify()` cell at the end of the notebook. It tests your own outputs against tolerances and
prints a completion code. If it fails, you have found your error while it is still cheap to fix —
that is the point of it. Paste the code into your submission.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 7 · Done looks like — the checklist your neighbour runs on you at minute 65

- [ ] Every lesson carries a data citation
- [ ] at least one remembered lesson is contradicted or unsupported
- [ ] the archive opens on a machine other than the author's
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 8 · Where it is saved

`IMSE456/studio-15/` in your cloud folder. Name files `SA14_yourlastname.*`.

**Nothing in this course is saved to a local disk.** Lab machines wipe on reboot and laptops get
left at home. Submit the PDF and the completion code to Blackboard by the due date above.
:::

::: {.browser-path}
**Working on lab machines?**

**No ProjectLibre?** Do the *Use* half in Smartsheet instead — indented WBS, Gantt, predecessors and critical path all work in a browser. Say so in your submission; it costs you nothing.

**No Antigravity?** Use the Gemini API from the course Colab notebook — the key is in the shared config cell. Same work, browser only.

**Power BI here is the browser Service** at [app.powerbi.com](https://app.powerbi.com). Nothing to install; works on any machine.
:::


::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Label it, verify it, own it.** Append the AI acknowledgement block from the [syllabus](../syllabus.qmd#how-to-disclose): the tool, the prompt or transcript link, what you changed after reviewing its output, and what it got wrong. Every quantitative result arrives with the check that proves it — **the check is graded, not the output**. "The model said so" is not a defence in this course or in a project review.
:::
